endorsements.quote: Authors are recommended to complete the checklist indicating the page number where each subitem has been reported.

Authors using generative AI models for medical writing are encouraged to apply the ChatGPT, Generative Artificial Intelligence, and Natural Large Language Models for Accountable Reporting and Use Guidelines (CANGARU) reporting guidelines, which are in development.

unlisted_practices: Clinical journals should adopt the CHART reporting standard for chatbot health advice studies.

Authors should report chatbot health advice studies using the CHART checklist, including model identifiers, prompt engineering, query strategy, reference standard, performance evaluation, and sample size.
Funders should invest in high-quality benchmarking and validation studies and rigorous chatbot health advice studies in the health care setting of interest.
Regulators should ensure generative AI developers put data security measures in place according to risk category.
Authors of chatbot health advice studies should report whether ethics approval was obtained, particularly when patients or the public are involved in prompt engineering or evaluation.
Authors of chatbot health advice studies should share code and training data sets to improve transparency and mitigate uncertainty over data provenance.
Authors should state whether permission or license was obtained for use of copyrighted data in chatbot health advice studies.
Researchers, ethicists, clinicians, and regulators should prioritize standardized quality validation metrics and validation methods for generative AI chatbots providing health advice.
Reporting guidelines for generative AI should be maintained as living guidelines with a dynamic process for monitoring and updating.

screen.reason: This paper presents a formal reporting guideline (CHART statement) developed via Delphi consensus for reporting generative AI chatbot health advice studies.
